Exercise A

Europe Working Together

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

The European Union, or EU, is a partnership of 27 European countries that work closely together. It began after the Second World War, when several countries decided to cooperate so that another war would be less likely. Over the years, more and more countries have joined, and the partnership has grown into one of the largest economies in the world.

Members of the EU trade freely with each other, which means that goods can move across borders without extra taxes. Citizens of EU countries can also live and work in any other member state. Many students, for example, have studied in other European countries thanks to exchange programmes such as Erasmus.

The United Kingdom joined the European Community in 1973. However, the relationship was not always easy, and many British people disagreed about how close the UK should be to the rest of Europe. In 2016, a referendum was held, and a small majority voted to leave. Since then, the UK has left the EU — a process that became known as "Brexit". Although the UK is no longer a member, it still trades with the EU and shares many close ties with its European neighbours.

Exercise D

Writing – Working Together

Write a paragraph (80–120 words): what are the advantages and disadvantages of countries working closely together, as they do in the EU? Give your opinion. Use the present perfect at least twice and at least three linking words.
